verified: The refactor in 1e8cc6e is behavior-preserving. `AgentControlHTTPRequest.parse` is the same, including the order of checks: header marker, headerLimit (tooLarge), UTF-8 and head (invalid), transfer-encoding (invalid), content-length (invalid), bodyLimit (tooLarge), then incomplete or complete. `head` and `length` are line-for-line extractions of the old code. The reason dictionary has the same 10 codes with the same default "Error".

`ipv6`, `ipv4Tail` and `groups` are equivalent to the old code. Checked cases: `::` gives 16 zero bytes; `::1` is accepted and is not tailnet; `fd7a:115c:a1e0::1` matches bytes 0 to 5; `::ffff:100.68.57.78` gives 6 groups plus 4 tail bytes and the CGNAT check; too many groups gives `missing < 1` and nil; a single half with fewer or more than 8 groups gives nil; `:::`, `1::2::3` and a malformed tail give nil. Dotted forms with no `ffff` group, such as `::1.2.3.4`, are rejected (fail closed). That was the same in the old code and is harmless.
The split test is fine. It does not change which assertions run, and both new test names are unique. Both tests are still valid when run separately.

Auth ordering is fine. Peer check first, then Origin (403), then credential: wrong path gives 404, bad key gives 401 with WWW-Authenticate, and a non-POST with a good key gives 405. Bearer wins over the path token. Token hashes are compared in constant time against every stored hash. The query string is ignored.

The code now does what the PR claims. Revoke: Remove calls `gate.set(nil)` and `tailnet.revoke`, which clears the hash, nils the plaintext and rebuilds the endpoint (per-client MCP server state is dropped, so the old approval state goes with it). Plaintext keys are never persisted: the store saves only hashes, the file is mode 0600, a failed load refuses every token and is never overwritten, and legacy plaintext tokens are migrated to hashes. Toggling off or turning the local socket off closes the sockets, the links and the endpoint. 413 and 400 are consistent between the code and docs/architecture.md.

reviews.scope: delta since 1e8cc6e (close links on address change, merge of #111)
verified: OutsideAgentsSettingsView.swift: the merge kept both calls. Remove runs gate.change(nil, for: client) and then listener.tailnet.revoke(client). The Picker setter also uses gate.change.

rebind() still returns early when the addresses, the listener count and the error state are unchanged: `if found == bound, listeners.count == found.count, error == nil { return }`. That line is untouched.

closeLinks() is safe when a link's close calls back into drop(_:). It copies links, empties the array, and only then closes each link. Link.close() is guarded by `open`, so it runs once, and its drop(_:) removes from the already-empty array and does nothing. Everything is @MainActor, so nothing else can touch `links` in between.

closeLinks() runs when the Tailscale addresses disappear, and when `found != bound` before listeners are recreated. The case where the address set is unchanged but the error is set (rebind retry) does not close links.

bind(_:port:) keeps the old loop unchanged: isTailnetPeer guard, the same NWParameters, handlers and start(queue: .main), listeners appended, last error returned. The caller still sets bound = found and the same error expression afterwards, so behaviour matches the old inline code. It compiles under Swift 6: both methods are @MainActor, and handlers hop through Task { @MainActor } with [weak self].
stopSockets() now calls closeLinks(), the same behaviour as the old inline code.
open_notes: When the address set changes, all links are closed, including ones on an address that is still bound. Clients reconnect, so this is acceptable.
